title: Execution Snapshot Railroad Visualizer - compact correlated drilldown for spans & timelines
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Engineers need a compact, scannable view that correlates spans across services for a single request trace while making it fast to identify the root cause, high-cost tokens, and anomalous latencies. Current trace detail pages are tall and require a lot of vertical scrolling and context switches between timeline and span list.

Goal: Deliver a prototype for a horizontal "railroad" style execution snapshot that condenses the full trace into a time-aligned rail, surface important attributes (status, error, cost estimate, model variant), and allow rapid keyboard and mouse drilldown to span details and logs. The view should interoperate with correlation ID search, filters (service, span-type, error), and Route/Model cost breakdown.

Scope: Design the primary desktop interactions, keyboard accessibility, hover & expand micro-interactions, grouping by service or tenant, and a compact mobile fallback. Provide a high-fidelity Figma prototype and annotated handoff for Eng with DOM and perf recommendations.

Success metrics: reduced mean time to investigate (MTTI) for traced incidents by 25% in usability study, 90% keyboard coverage, and engineering signoff that initial rendering keeps DOM node count < 1200 for 10k-span traces via lazy-expansion strategy.
design_decisions: Use a horizontally time-aligned 'railroad' visualization with fixed time axis and stacked lanes per service to make cross-service timing immediately visible.
Encode span outcomes with three visual states: normal (muted blue), warning (amber), error (red). Errors get a pulsing subtle attention state on first render.
Compact spans use width-proportional rectangles with truncated labels and a hover card showing full metadata and direct links to logs/trace permalink.
Adopt progressive disclosure: render only top-level spans per lane by default, with 'expand siblings' and 'expand subtree' affordances to prevent DOM bloat.
Map cost attribution to a thin right-aligned bar per span showing relative token/cost impact; tooltip with per-token estimate and model variant.
Provide keyboard-first navigation: arrow keys for lane/time movement, Enter to open span details, '/' to focus correlation search, 'F' to apply quick filters.
Design provides two grouping modes: Service-grouped and Category-grouped (e.g., 'inference', 'db', 'cache') selectable from the header.
Accessibility: color does not convey status alone; add status icons and accessible labels for screen readers; ensure 4.5:1 contrast for critical states.
Mobile fallback: stacked lanes collapse into a vertical stacked timeline with touch affordances; heavy traces show a summarized 'heatline' strip with tap-to-expand.
Tradeoff: a fully-dense waterfall with inline logs is deferred to a secondary panel to keep the visualizer performant and maintainable.
Telemetry: capture expand/collapse events, filter usage, and time-to-first-click on an error span for future iteration.
Performance constraint: request that Eng implement virtualized rails and span element recycling; initial target first-paint < 300ms on typical 4-core developer machines.
Interoperability: each span hover card will include a 'Jump to Console Trace View' and 'Open model call in Debugger' links for cross-surface context.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype linked in attachments demonstrates service-grouped and category-grouped modes with working hover cards and keyboard navigation flows.
Annotated handoff lists DOM/perf constraints and lazy-load rules; Eng confirms feasibility and signs off in PRD comment thread.
Design review feedback addressed: contrast adjustments, iconography alignment with Console core, and copy for hover cards updated.
Usability micro-study (5 engineering participants) shows at least 3/5 complete a simulated investigation task faster than with current trace view.
Prototype includes accessibility notes and a11y checklist; keyboard navigation covers 90% of flows and screen reader labels present for key elements.
Links to sample trace permalink and synthetic trace data used for prototype are included in attachments for validation.
A minimal CSS spec for the railroad lanes and span sizing is added to the handoff doc.
PM confirms product alignment and adds release tag console-2025.02 to ticket.
Dependencies with ENG and PM are enumerated and acknowledged in comments.
Security review flagged if span metadata may surface PII; no PII surfaced in current prototype per review notes.
Design tokens and color variables reference existing Console theme tokens to avoid drift.
Acceptance demo recorded and uploaded to attachments.
Optional: initial telemetry events instrumented by ENG on staging trace dataset.
